content:
Aiyana Brooks-Tan
Frontend Developer | React, TypeScript & Node.js
Dublin, Ireland | aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404
GitHub: github.com/aiyana-bt-example | Portfolio: aiyana-bt.example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Computing graduate and frontend developer with experience building React and Next.js web applications. Skilled in TypeScript, accessibility improvements, reusable components and automated unit testing. Technical skills also include Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3
Frontend: React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, Storybook, Figma
Backend and databases: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL
Testing and tools: Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub
Accessibility: WCAG 2.1

EXPERIENCE
Frontend Developer (part-time, freelance) | Self-employed
Oct 2025–Present
- Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS, hosted on Vercel.
- Made small updates to two WordPress sites.

Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media, Dublin
May 2024–Aug 2024
- Contributed to the company’s React news site as part of the web team.
- Fixed accessibility issues identified in an audit, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels, across 20+ components.
- Built a reusable image gallery component and created Storybook stories for it.
- Wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library.

Barista | Corner Bean Cafe, Dublin
2021–2025 | Part-time during studies

EDUCATION
BSc (Hons) Computing – Software Development | Liffey Institute of Technology
2021–2025 | First Class Honours
- Final-year project: “Tidewatch,” an accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers, built with React, TypeScript and Node.js.
- Relevant modules: Web Development, Databases, Human-Computer Interaction, Software Testing, Data Structures & Algorithms.

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Mandarin (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, concise, professionally structured, and easy to scan. The summary accurately presents the candidate as a frontend developer, while the experience bullets include useful evidence such as accessibility work across 20+ components, reusable components, Storybook, and unit testing. The First Class Honours degree and Tidewatch project are relevant. The main content limitation is that the CV presents a relatively short professional history for a role requiring 2+ years and does not provide concrete evidence of backend-service development, security knowledge, end-to-end testing, or responsive and semantic HTML work. The document should not imply these capabilities unless supported by the candidate's actual experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience, searchable technology names, and a simple text-based structure that should parse well in most ATS platforms. It includes strong matches such as React, TypeScript, Next.js, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, WCAG 2.1, Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub, Storybook, and Vercel. AI screening probability is moderate: the document will likely be recognized as a strong junior frontend profile, but may be filtered or ranked lower for this full-stack role because it does not explicitly demonstrate 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, backend-service delivery, end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals, or health-data privacy awareness. Do not add unsupported keywords merely to improve ATS matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the frontend and accessibility aspects of the role. It shows React, TypeScript, Next.js, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, automated unit testing, Git/GitHub, Storybook, and a wellness-related booking website. The internship's accessibility audit work is particularly relevant to Verdane Care's emphasis on accessible patient-facing software. The candidate's material does not establish 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, backend-service development, semantic HTML and responsive-layout knowledge, web security fundamentals, or health-data privacy experience. It also does not show German or Croatian, AWS, Docker, analytics, or A/B testing. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting. English is shown as native, and the CV demonstrates a credible junior-level match for the frontend, accessibility, and wellness-related aspects of the role.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified. The CV does not contain clear unsupported skills or experiences when cross-referenced with the Original Candidate Information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the strongest evidence more specific by changing the second sentence to: "Skilled in TypeScript, accessible and reusable React components, WCAG 2.1 improvements, Storybook, and automated unit testing with Jest and React Testing Library." This uses the candidate's documented evidence rather than leaving "accessibility improvements" and "automated unit testing" broad.
2. In the freelance Frontend Developer entry, keep the existing facts but make the project technology easier for ATS and recruiters to connect to the target role by changing the first bullet to: "Built and deployed a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS; hosted it on Vercel." Do not add React, TypeScript, API, database, payment, or authentication claims because they are not stated in the Original Candidate Information.
3. In the Software Development Intern entry, preserve the quantified accessibility evidence and make the testing technology more prominent by changing the final two bullets to: "Built a reusable image gallery component and created Storybook stories for it." and "Wrote unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library." These are already accurate, but the wording should remain explicit and should not be compressed into a generic "testing" or "component development" statement.
4. In the Education section, format the Tidewatch item as a clearly searchable project entry without adding new claims: "Final-year project — Tidewatch: accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers | React, TypeScript, Node.js." This gives the Node.js experience greater visibility while accurately presenting it as an academic project rather than professional backend-service experience.
5. In the Technical Skills section, retain the current category structure and use the job's supported terminology where accurate: change "Accessibility: WCAG 2.1" to "Web accessibility: WCAG 2.1" and retain "Testing and tools: Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub." Do not add WCAG 2.2, Playwright, NestJS, Docker, AWS, OWASP, authentication, GDPR, or health-data privacy because these are not supported by the candidate information.
